main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Trapped by Polyphemus, Odysseus uses wine, a false name, a stake, and the sheep to escape. He later reveals his identity in a boast, allowing the Cyclops to invoke Poseidon against him.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “I will tell it you; give me, therefore, the present you promised me; my name is Noman; this is what my father and mother and my friends have always called me.’ “But the cruel wretch said, ‘Then I will eat all Noman’s comrades before Noman himself, and will keep Noman for the last. This is the present”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The trick works because Polyphemus can repeat only the wrong information. Cunning here is control over words, timing, and the enemy's expectations.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Separate the successful escape plan from the later boast. Secrecy helps the crew survive; declaring his name satisfies Odysseus’ desire for recognition but creates a new danger.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Compare this with Achilles: Odysseus wins by temporary invisibility, not public honor.

quiz.prompt: What helps Odysseus conceal who attacked the Cyclops?
quiz.explanation: A false name. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: How does the later boast undermine the escape?

choices.text: It returns the stolen sheep to the cave.
It gives Polyphemus the identity needed for his curse.
It wakes the Cyclops before the men leave the cave.
